text:
jess: FYI AcmePay (dedicated-west-2) opened a severity-2 — p99 for /v1/generate jumped from ~600ms to ~3.2s starting ~08:30 UTC. Customer reports intermittent 500s as well. I see a few OOMs on the node. Can eng help triage?

devon: Which node pool? do we have pod/node ids and any recent deploys?

jess: Pool dedicated-west-2-gpu-a. Pod ids: gen-5f4c (tenant acmepay), gen-5f4c-2026-03-17T08:27 (rolled by autoscaler). No customer config changes.

infra-bot: Alert: GPU memory OOM events detected on host gpu-wn-12 at 2026-03-17T08:29:42Z (3 events in 6m).

sam: Pinging gpu-wn-12 — grabbing nvidia-smi and allocator stats.

sam: ```
GPU 0: 32GiB total, processes: model-server(28.2GiB), helper(0.5GiB)
Memory usage: 88%
No obvious GPU ECC errors.```

maria: Grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/latency/cluster-p99?var=node=gpu-wn-12&from=now-2h - shows steady p50 but p99 spikes aligned with OOMs and CPU steal on the host.

sam: Pulled heap/sbrk and allocator logs from the pod: ```
[2026-03-17T08:28:50Z] kv_cache: entries=1_024_512 size=8.1GiB
[2026-03-17T08:29:01Z] allocator: failed_alloc 1.2GiB -> triggered OOM slow-path
[2026-03-17T08:29:40Z] slab_frag: 22% fragmentation delta +8% in 3m
[2026-03-17T08:29:42Z] OOM: triggered cgroup kill (killed pid 17432)
```

devon: Looks like KV growth + fragmentation. Is prefix cache eviction disabled for AcmePay?

jess: Their tenant config shows prefix_cache.max_entries=1_500_000 and eviction_ratio=0.6 — nothing unusual. Historically they have big prompt sets so KV grows.

elaine: Can we repro locally with their traffic profile? Maybe a load generator hitting multi-turn long-context sequences.

sam: I replayed a subset of their workload against a staging node: within ~5-7 minutes observed same allocator slow-paths and p99 jumps. Repro steps: ```
1) start model-server with --kv-max-entries=1_500_000 --allocator=bfc
2) run loadgen --threads=32 --seq-len=2048 --profile=acmepay.json
3) watch /metrics for kv_cache_entries and allocator_failed_allocs
```

marcus: Short-term mitigation: lower kv eviction threshold and enable soft-kv-evict. I suggest pushing a config patch to the node: kv_cache.eviction_ratio -> 0.4 and kv_cache.soft_evict=true for AcmePay, then drain heavy pods to force reallocation.

devon: Agreed. Also bump allocator defrag frequency: set allocator.defrag_interval=30s (was 5m) and reduce bfc_growth_limit to 0.12 to avoid large transient allocations.

jess: Applying temp config to tenant in staging now. Will roll to dedicated-west-2 after verification.

support-bot: Logged action: ticket #SUP-4829 updated — mitigation in progress. Notifying customer of temporary traffic routing while we triage.

maria: After staging change, p99 dropped from 3.2s -> 720ms in the repro. Fragmentation delta stabilized to <3% over 10m.

sam: Commands I ran to inspect on host: ```
# check cgroup memory
cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/kubepods.slice/.../memory.stat
# check slabinfo
cat /proc/slabinfo | egrep "slab|kv_cache"
# live kv sizes
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9090/metrics | grep kv_cache
```

elaine: Next steps (owner in parens):
- Roll tenant config to dedicated-west-2 (jess)
- Increase monitoring alert granularity for kv_cache growth (maria)
- Add an autoscaling policy to shift heavy tenants to larger GPU types on sustained kv growth (devon)
- Schedule allocator tuning release with runtime team for persistent fix (elaine)

marcus: FYI we should also consider adding a soft OOM throttle that slows acceptance of new requests once allocator failed_allocs > 3 in 1m to protect p99 for other tenants. I'll draft a proposal.

jess: Customer notified: "We identified GPU memory fragmentation + KV growth as root cause. Applying temporary eviction and allocator tuning; expect latency to improve within 10-15m. We'll follow up with permanent mitigations." :white_check_mark:

support-bot: Ticket #SUP-4829 updated to status: fix-in-progress. ETA next update 09:15 UTC.
